rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=False, train_n=400, n_iter=60, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.003, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=iter-17 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: warm_start True->False (pure per-image N2I, NO amortised pre-pass), on the CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, lr=3e-3, n_iter=60; iter-15 hr=0.2056). n_iter held at 60 (iter-16 n_iter90 hr=0.2051 = TIED -> the 6-param BF converges by 60, saturated). HYPOTHESIS: the warm-start pre-pass captures a GENERIC BF-sigma init from the 400 train scenes; but the per-scene fit already tunes sigmas per image, so warm-start may add a generic-abdomen bias the tight img_sr must undo. With warm_start=False each scene fits from the CONFIG init (img_sr=0.0002 exactly) -> if hr >= 0.2056 the warm-start is UNNECESSARY (pure per-image N2I is self-sufficient AND drops the train-set dependency, a cleaner self-supervised story: train_n=0); if hr DROPS, the warm-start init genuinely helps the 60-step fit converge and should be kept. Either outcome is a clean methodological finding for the paper. WALL: skipping warm-start SAVES ~120s -> n_iter60 fits comfortably, val_n~200 (outer_wall_s=1000). ONE knob: warm_start True->False.
